errors.rationale: This CSS matching boundary neither calls a throwing method nor creates an error result; the observable result in the page's table is whether an existing pseudo-class matches an element.

securityPrivacy.rationale: The selector matching boundary changes rendering styles in response to user action; the cited spec and ChromeStatus description introduce no new permission, data access, or privacy-sensitive output.

notes: B3 unit: added only three heading ids and linked the two named sources in the previously unlinked 'the rule' citation. This is one collective CSS matching behavior, not three new pseudo-classes; the #syntax table documents the element-state outcomes, #examples contains an existing semantic CSS code block, and #compatibility holds the existing browser table. SOURCE/PAGE DISAGREEMENTS (fetched 2026-10-07; neither side adjudicated, disclosure and pin drafted for implementer, not written on page): the page's at-a-glance Status is 'Enabled by default' and calls this 'Shipped in' Chrome 149 / Edge 149, while the ChromeStatus feature API reports chrome.status.text 'Proposed' (chrome.desktop/android/webview milestone 149, flag false, origintrial false). Separately, the page describes pseudo-class propagation 'upward through the DOM' and says 'all its ancestors match too', whereas CSS Selectors Level 4 §useraction-pseudos specifies propagation on 'flat tree ancestors' only, up to and including the first top layer element or the root, whichever is first; those tree scopes are not equivalent in shadow DOM. MDN's linked :hover reference is a general selector reference, not evidence of this Chrome 149 behavior change; its former URL redirected, so all three outdated MDN selector links were repaired to their live canonical CSS Reference paths, and this contract source URL was updated with the page. The mail-archive PSA confirms the feature, while the normative flat-tree rule comes from CSS Selectors Level 4.
